text: For each of the 13 building blocks, I can name the signal that justifies it, its main cost, and the Phase 1–6 lesson that covers it.
I can say a block and its watch-out in the same sentence, with the number from estimation that triggered it.
I can choose between cache and read replica, queue and log, SQL and NoSQL, and replication and sharding, by comparing what each holds, what it answers and how it fails.
I can quote a planning figure for each block from earlier lessons, label it as an assumption, and use it to decide whether the block is needed.
I can run a case study's estimates through the table and show which blocks the numbers rule out, as in the URL-shortener example.
I can name at least one case study where each block is the decisive choice, and one where the obvious block was deliberately not used.
